mainTopic: Whether a five-טפחים embankment (גידוד) and a five-טפחים partition (מחיצה) combine to make a ten-טפחים separation, and how this affects עירוב between two courtyards at different heights.
overview: רב חסדא rules that five טפחים of embankment (גידוד) and five טפחים of wall (מחיצה) do not combine into a ten-טפחים barrier. The גמרא challenges him from a ברייתא about an upper and a lower courtyard, and defends him by explaining the ברייתא's cases one step at a time: the barrier looks like a full wall from below, the upper courtyard had side walls that make the gap a doorway, and the lower courtyard was open along its whole width. In the end the סיפא is read as speaking only about the lower courtyard. Then מרימר teaches the opposite ruling: embankment and partition do combine. רב אחא has no tradition against this, and the גמרא rules like מרימר. Next, רב הושעיא asks whether residents who join a courtyard on שבת itself forbid carrying there. רב חסדא tries to prove that they do from the משנה of a large courtyard breached into a small one. רבה and אביי reject the proof, because of the rule that once שבת began permitted, it stays permitted. Finally, the גמרא brings a dispute about a wall between two courtyards that fell on שבת: רב allows carrying only within four אמות, and שמואל's view begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Embankment and partition do not combine
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that a five-טפחים embankment and a five-טפחים wall cannot join to make a ten-טפחים barrier. The barrier must be entirely one kind or entirely the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: An embankment of five and a partition of five do not combine, unless it is either entirely embankment or entirely partition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states רב חסדא's rule: a barrier made of half natural drop (גידוד) and half built wall (מחיצה) does not count as a ten-טפחים מחיצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A halachic מחיצה must be ten טפחים tall. רב חסדא holds that two different kinds of barrier cannot be added together to reach that height. Only a full ten of one kind works.

keyTerms.meaning: An embankment; a drop in ground level between two surfaces
Handbreadths; ten are needed for a valid partition

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the base rule that the next steps test and defend. However, מרימר disagrees in step 10, and the final הלכה in step 13 rules against רב חסדא.

phrases.english: An embankment of five handbreadths and a partition of five
phrases.notes: The statement belongs to רב חסדא, whose name appears on the previous amud.

phrases.english: do not combine
unless it is either entirely embankment
or entirely partition.

steps.triggerLanguage: גִּידּוּד חֲמִשָּׁה וּמְחִיצָה חֲמִשָּׁה אֵין מִצְטָרְפִין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five טפחים of embankment plus five טפחים of partition do not form a valid ten-טפחים מחיצה.

steps.title: A ברייתא about two courtyards at different heights
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if the upper courtyard is higher by ten, or by five of embankment plus five of wall, each courtyard makes its own עירוב. This suggests 5+5 does combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: Two courtyards, one above the other, where the upper is ten handbreadths higher than the lower, or it has an embankment of five and a partition of five, make two עירובין and not one. If the difference is less than this, they make one עירוב and not two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא from a ברייתא that treats 5 embankment plus 5 wall exactly like a full ten-טפחים separation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making two separate עירובין means the courtyards count as two separate domains. That only happens if there is a valid ten-טפחים מחיצה between them. Since the ברייתא says 5+5 creates that separation, it seems to contradict רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: The upper courtyard and the lower courtyard

steps.confusionAlert: 'Two עירובין' means the courtyards are separate. 'One עירוב' means they are joined as one domain.

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי: שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵירוֹת זוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזּוֹ
phrases.english: They challenged: Two courtyards, one above the other,

phrases.aramaic: וְעֶלְיוֹנָה גְּבוֹהָה מִן הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים,
phrases.english: and the upper one is ten handbreadths higher than the lower,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ גִּידּוּד חֲמִשָּׁה וּמְחִיצָה חֲמִשָּׁה —
phrases.english: or it has an embankment of five and a partition of five
they make two עירובין, and do not make one.
Less than this,
they make one עירוב, and do not make two!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that embankment and partition do not combine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats 5 embankment plus 5 partition as a full separation that requires two עירובין, so they do combine.

steps.title: רב חסדא agrees from the lower courtyard's view
steps.stepSummary: The first answer: רב חסדא agrees that 5+5 counts for the lower courtyard, because its residents look up at a full ten-טפחים face.
steps.simpleTranslation: (רב) said: רב חסדא agrees regarding the lower courtyard, since it faces a wall of ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא. His rule applies to the upper side, but from the lower courtyard the barrier counts as a full ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone standing in the lower courtyard sees one continuous surface ten טפחים tall: five of earth topped by five of wall. So for the lower courtyard it is a real מחיצה. From the upper courtyard, only the five-טפחים wall is visible, so רב חסדא's rule still applies there.

keyTerms.meaning: Faces a surface of ten טפחים

phrases.english: (Rav) said: Rav Chisda agrees regarding the lower courtyard,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the name in round brackets, so it isn't clear who said this.

phrases.english: since it faces a wall of ten.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule to one side (perspective-based distinction).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to show that 5+5 combines in every way, against רב חסדא.
steps.terutzMaskana: 5+5 combines only from the lower courtyard's view. רב חסדא's rule stands for the upper courtyard.

steps.title: Then the upper courtyard could make no עירוב at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the answer. If only the lower side is separated, the upper courtyard can neither join the lower one nor make its own עירוב, but the ברייתא says both make עירובין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so: the lower courtyard should make two and not one, and the upper courtyard should make neither one nor two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer in step 3 by working out what it means for the upper courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the upper courtyard the wall is only five טפחים, so it is open toward the lower courtyard and has no proper enclosure for its own עירוב. Yet it cannot join the lower courtyard either, because the lower one is walled off from it. The ברייתא says simply 'two עירובין', implying that both courtyards can make one.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is the case
It (the courtyard) should make an עירוב

phrases.english: If so:

phrases.aramaic: תַּחְתּוֹנָה — תְּעָרֵב שְׁנַיִם וְלֹא תְּעָרֵב אֶחָד,
phrases.english: the lower should make two and not make one,

phrases.aramaic: עֶלְיוֹנָה — לֹא תְּעָרֵב לֹא אֶחָד וְלֹא שְׁנַיִם.
phrases.english: the upper should make neither one nor two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that רב חסדא agrees only for the lower courtyard.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That view leaves the upper courtyard unable to make any עירוב, but the ברייתא gives both courtyards two עירובין.

steps.title: The upper courtyard had full walls on its sides
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא explains the case: the upper courtyard had full ten-טפחים walls on both sides of the short section, which was no more than ten אמות wide. The short section therefore counts as a doorway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר עולא said: The case is where the upper courtyard was walled in, up to ten cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר עולא answers the last question by describing the exact setup the ברייתא is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An opening of up to ten אמות in a properly walled area counts as a פתח (doorway), not a breach. So the upper courtyard is fully enclosed and can make its own עירוב. The lower courtyard faces a full ten-טפחים wall with no doorway into the upper one, so they cannot share one עירוב, and each makes its own.

keyTerms.meaning: For example; the case is where
Walled in or enclosed on its sides
Ten cubits, the maximum width of an opening that still counts as a doorway

steps.whatToRemember: For now, רב חסדא's rule survives the challenge. The ברייתא's 5+5 works only because it is a full wall from below, and because the upper courtyard's side walls turn the short section into a doorway. Step 13 later rules against רב חסדא.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Ulla said:
For example, where the upper courtyard was walled in
up to ten cubits.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The upper courtyard was thought to be open and unable to make any עירוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The upper courtyard is enclosed by side walls, and the short section counts as a פתח of up to ten אמות. Each courtyard makes its own עירוב.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא does not fit the doorway explanation
steps.stepSummary: If the short section works as a doorway, the courtyards should be allowed to choose one עירוב or two. But the סיפא says that below ten they make only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the end of the ברייתא: 'If it is less than this, they make one עירוב and do not make two.' But according to your explanation, they should be able to make one if they want, or two if they want!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה בר עולא's doorway explanation using the last line (סיפא) of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר עולא said the upper courtyard had full ten-טפחים walls with a short gap that counts as a doorway. Two courtyards joined by a doorway may choose one shared עירוב or two separate ones. So why does the סיפא force them to make only one?

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your explanation is correct)
The last clause of a משנה or ברייתא
Less than this (less than ten טפחים)

phrases.english: If so, say the latter clause:
Less than this —
they make one eiruv, and they do not make two,
but if it wishes, let it make one,
and if it wishes, let it make two!
phrases.notes: This is the normal rule for two courtyards with a doorway between them

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה בר עולא's doorway explanation from Step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר עולא's explanation that the short section counts as a doorway
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A doorway allows the courtyards to choose one עירוב or two. The סיפא forbids two, so the doorway setup does not match the סיפא.

steps.title: The lower courtyard was open along its whole width
steps.stepSummary: רבה בריה דרבא explains that the whole width of the lower courtyard was open to the upper one. The lower courtyard therefore counts as part of the upper one and cannot make its own עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה, the son of רבא, said: The case is where the lower courtyard was breached along its full width into the upper courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בריה דרבא answers the challenge by describing the exact setup of the סיפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סיפא, the lower courtyard's entire side is open to the upper courtyard, which is wider. There is an earlier rule that when a big courtyard is breached into a small one, the small one is absorbed into the big one. So the small, lower courtyard cannot make its own עירוב and must join the upper one.
steps.confusionAlert: Only the smaller courtyard, the one opened along its full width, loses its independence. The bigger courtyard does not. This one-way rule is what drives the next step.

phrases.english: Rabba, son of Rava, said:
For example, where the lower one was breached
along its full width into the upper one.
phrases.notes: Based on the rule of a big courtyard breached into a small one

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא כְּגוֹן שֶׁנִּפְרְצָה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא describes a doorway, where the courtyards may choose
steps.terutzMaskana: The lower courtyard is fully open to the upper one, so it is absorbed and cannot make its own עירוב

steps.title: Then only the lower courtyard should be limited
steps.stepSummary: If that is the case, only the lower courtyard is limited to one עירוב. The upper courtyard should still be allowed to choose one or two.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the lower courtyard makes one עירוב and cannot make two. But the upper courtyard may make two if it wishes, or one if it wishes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem with the new explanation. The ברייתא's wording seems to limit both courtyards, but this setup limits only one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'big into small' rule works in one direction. The small courtyard is absorbed, but the big one keeps its independence. So the upper courtyard should keep its freedom to choose, yet the ברייתא sounds like it limits everyone.

phrases.english: If so, the lower one makes one eiruv,
it does not make two.
The upper one, if it wishes, makes two,
and if it wishes, makes one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what Step 7's setup implies and contrasts it with the ברייתא's wording
steps.kashyaTarget: The general wording of the סיפא, read together with רבה בריה דרבא's setup
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The breach rule limits only the smaller courtyard, but the ברייתא seems to limit both

steps.title: The ruling of the סיפא refers only to the lower courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that the upper courtyard may choose. It explains that 'one and not two' was said only about the lower courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so. When the ברייתא teaches 'less than this, they make one עירוב and not two,' it refers to the lower courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the point raised in Step 8. It resolves the problem by narrowing whom the סיפא is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of rejecting רבה בריה דרבא, the גמרא reads the סיפא as aimed at the lower courtyard alone. The upper courtyard keeps its choice. The ברייתא now fits the breach rule fully.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, it is indeed so (agreeing with the point)

steps.whatToRemember: Here is how the whole ברייתא is now explained. With ten טפחים of difference, the upper courtyard has a doorway setup, so both courtyards make their own עירובין. With less than ten, the lower courtyard is fully open to the upper one, so only the lower courtyard is limited to one shared עירוב. The upper courtyard may choose.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so.
And when it teaches
'Less than this, they make one eiruv
and do not make two,'
it refers to the lower one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts Step 8's point and reinterprets the ברייתא's wording
steps.terutzResolutionType: Agrees with the objection and narrows the ברייתא's wording to one courtyard
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא limits both courtyards to one עירוב
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא limits only the lower courtyard. The upper one may choose one or two.

steps.title: מרימר: Five of Embankment Plus Five of Partition Combine
steps.stepSummary: מרימר teaches that a five-טפחים embankment and a five-טפחים partition on top of it join together to make a valid ten-טפחים divider.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר taught: an embankment of five and a partition of five combine.
steps.whatsHappening: מרימר teaches a new rule about how to reach the required height of ten טפחים. A drop in the ground can be added to a wall built on top of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the exact opposite of רב חסדא's rule in step 1 (גידוד חמשה ומחיצה חמשה אין מצטרפין). מרימר holds that the two kinds of barrier can be mixed: five טפחים of embankment plus five טפחים of built wall count as one ten-טפחים divider.

keyTerms.meaning: taught publicly, gave a public lecture
an embankment, a sharp rise or drop in the ground

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule becomes the final הלכה in step 13. It means that a partition built on top of a ground-level drop counts toward the full ten-טפחים height.

phrases.english: Mareimar taught publicly:
An embankment of five (handbreadths) and a partition of five (handbreadths)
phrases.notes: The partition stands on top of the embankment.

phrases.english: combine (to make ten).
phrases.notes: Together they count as one ten-טפחים divider.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the rule of step 1 and gives the opposing view: embankment and partition do combine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A five-טפחים embankment and a five-טפחים partition combine to make ten טפחים.

steps.title: רבינא Asks רב אחא Whether He Learned Anything About This Partition
steps.stepSummary: רבינא meets רב אחא בריה דרבא and asks whether he has a tradition about this kind of combined partition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא met רב אחא the son of רבא and said to him: Did the master learn anything about this partition?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא checks whether anyone has an older teaching about combining an embankment and a partition. The גמרא is setting up a short answer before it rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא wants to know whether there is an earlier source that agrees or disagrees with מרימר. If there were an opposing tradition, it could affect the final ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: he met him, he found him
did the master learn (a teaching) anything?

phrases.aramaic: אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא,
phrases.english: Ravina met Rav Acha the son of Rava,
he said to him:
Did the master learn anything about (this) partition?
phrases.notes: He means the combined embankment-and-partition case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for an earlier tradition about מרימר's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is there an earlier teaching about whether an embankment and a partition combine?

steps.title: רב אחא Answers That He Has No Tradition
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא answers that he did not learn anything about it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא says he has no teaching on the subject. No tradition from him supports רב חסדא against מרימר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because no opposing tradition exists, the way is open for the גמרא to accept מרימר's rule as the final ruling.

phrases.english: He said to him: No.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is no earlier tradition on this question.

steps.title: The Final Ruling: Embankment and Partition Combine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה follows מרימר: five of embankment and five of partition combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: an embankment of five and a partition of five combine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final ruling and accepts מרימר's rule as הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא rules like מרימר and against רב חסדא's rule in step 1. רב אחא had no tradition that would support רב חסדא. A mixed barrier made of a five-טפחים drop and a five-טפחים wall counts as a full divider.
steps.whatToRemember: A five-טפחים גידוד and a five-טפחים מחיצה combine to make a valid ten-טפחים divider. This is the הלכה.

phrases.english: And the הלכה is:
an embankment of five and a partition of five
combine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute between רב חסדא (step 1) and מרימר (step 10) in favor of מרימר.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is that a five-טפחים embankment and a five-טפחים partition combine.

steps.title: Do Residents Who Arrive on שבת Forbid Carrying?
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא asks whether people who become residents of a courtyard on שבת itself make carrying there forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא asked: residents who arrive on שבת, do they make (carrying) forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. Suppose a wall falls on שבת and people from the next courtyard suddenly share this courtyard. Do these new residents forbid carrying there?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, residents who did not join the עירוב forbid carrying in a shared courtyard. The question is whether this also applies when they only became residents during שבת. Another way to ask it: is the status of the courtyard fixed when שבת begins?

keyTerms.meaning: he asked a question that needs to be resolved

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya asked:
Residents who arrive on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: For example, a wall between two courtyards falls down on שבת.

phrases.english: what is (the law), do they make (carrying) forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic that is connected to the case of a breached courtyard.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do residents who join a courtyard on שבת itself make carrying there forbidden?

steps.title: רב חסדא's Proof from the Large and Small Courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא brings the משנה that when a large courtyard is breached into a small one, the small one is forbidden. He understands this to include a breach on שבת, so new residents do forbid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said, come and hear: a large courtyard that was breached into a small one, the large one is permitted and the small one is forbidden, because it is like the doorway of the large one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא tries to answer רב הושעיא's question from a משנה. The small courtyard becomes forbidden because of the breach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not say when the breach happened. רב חסדא assumes it covers a breach on שבת too. If so, people who suddenly share the small courtyard on שבת still make carrying forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: Only the small courtyard is forbidden. The large one stays permitted, because the breach just looks like one of its doorways.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said, come and hear:
a large courtyard that was breached into a small one —
the large one is permitted and the small one is forbidden,
because it (the breach) is like the doorway of the large one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer רב הושעיא's question from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: Residents who arrive on שבת do make carrying forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of a large courtyard breached into a small one, read as covering a breach on שבת.

steps.title: רבה: Maybe the Breach Happened Before שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבה rejects the proof by suggesting the משנה is talking about a breach that happened on Friday.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Say that it was breached while it was still day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה pushes back on רב חסדא's proof. The משנה may be talking about a breach that happened before שבת began.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the breach happened on Friday, the residents were already sharing the courtyard when שבת began. The משנה would then tell us nothing about residents who arrive during שבת, so this proof does not settle רב הושעיא's question. Steps 17-18 strengthen this rejection.

keyTerms.meaning: while it was still day, before שבת

phrases.english: Rabba said:
Say that it was breached while it was still day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: אֵימַר מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם נִפְרְצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב חסדא's proof by narrowing the case of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the משנה about the breached courtyard.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the breach happened on שבת. It may have happened before שבת.

steps.title: אביי: Not 'Maybe', but Certainly Before שבת
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רבה not to say 'maybe'. The משנה must be talking about a breach before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Let the master not say 'say (perhaps)'. Rather, it was certainly breached while it was still day.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי strengthens רבה's rejection. He says the Friday reading is not just possible but required. The proof for this comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה offered the Friday reading only as a possibility. אביי argues it is the only possible reading, which removes רב חסדא's proof completely.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Let the master not say 'say (perhaps)',
rather, it was certainly breached while it was still day.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא מָר אֵימַר, אֶלָּא וַדַּאי
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב חסדא's proof from the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה cannot be about a breach on שבת at all.

steps.title: אביי's Proof: Once שבת Was Permitted, It Stays Permitted
steps.stepSummary: אביי proves his point from רבה's own report. רב הונא or רב יהודה told him that if carrying was permitted when שבת began, closing the opening later does not take that permission away.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the master is the one who said: I asked רב הונא and I asked רב יהודה: if someone made an עירוב through a doorway and the doorway was sealed, or through a window and the window was sealed, what is the law? And he said to me: שבת, once it was permitted, it was permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי reminds רבה of a ruling רבה himself reported. The status at the start of שבת stays in place for the whole שבת. So a breach during שבת could not make the small courtyard forbidden, and the משנה must mean a breach before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule שבת כיון שהותרה הותרה means a change during שבת does not undo a permission that was in place when שבת began. If the משנה were about a breach on שבת, the small courtyard would stay permitted. Since the משנה calls it forbidden, it must be talking about a breach on Friday.

keyTerms.meaning: for the master himself is the one who said
he made an עירוב through the doorway
and it was sealed, closed up
once שבת began permitted, it stays permitted

steps.whatToRemember: שבת כיון שהותרה הותרה: the status at the start of שבת stays in place. That is why the משנה of the breached courtyard must be about a breach before שבת, and it cannot answer רב הושעיא's question.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is the key to the whole question about residents who arrive on שבת. It points toward the view that new arrivals during שבת do not take away a permission that already existed.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. In רבה's case the courtyards were permitted and then a doorway closed. In רב הושעיא's case, new residents join. The shared idea is that the status at the start of שבת stays in place.

phrases.english: For the master is the one who said:
I asked Rav Huna
and I asked Rav Yehuda:
(If) one made an עירוב through the doorway and the doorway was sealed,
phrases.notes: The doorway was sealed on שבת.

phrases.aramaic: עֵירַב דֶּרֶךְ חַלּוֹן וְנִסְתַּם הַחַלּוֹן, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: (or) made an עירוב through a window and the window was sealed, what is (the law)?
And he said to me:
Shabbat, once it was permitted, it was permitted.
phrases.notes: The permission stays for the rest of שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the proof for אביי's claim that the breach must have happened before שבת.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה of the breached courtyard must be about a breach before שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה's own report of the ruling שבת כיון שהותרה הותרה, which he heard from רב הונא or רב יהודה.

steps.title: רב's ruling on a wall that collapsed on Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a dispute about a wall between two courtyards that fell on שבת. רב rules that carrying is allowed only within four אמות. The גמרא then begins to quote שמואל's opposing view.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: If a wall between two courtyards collapsed on שבת, רב said that one may carry there only within four אמות. And שמואל said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new אמוראים dispute. It gives רב's ruling first and then sets up שמואל's opposing view, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before שבת each courtyard was closed off and carrying inside it was permitted. On שבת the wall fell, so the two courtyards became one open space without a shared עירוב. רב says carrying now becomes forbidden, except for the small four-אמות area. This means רב does not accept the rule from the last step that 'what was permitted when שבת began stays permitted.'

keyTerms.meaning: One may carry or move objects
Four cubits. This is the small area where one may always carry, even where carrying is otherwise forbidden.

steps.confusionAlert: The courtyards were permitted when שבת began. רב still forbids carrying because of the change that happened on שבת. Do not assume everyone agrees that permission from the start of שבת lasts all day. רב does not hold that way.
steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute ties directly to the earlier question about changes on שבת, like new residents or a breach. רב's view shows there is a real opinion that goes against the rule אביי just quoted.

phrases.english: It was stated:
phrases.notes: This signals a dispute between אמוראים.

phrases.english: A wall that is between two courtyards and that collapsed,
phrases.notes: It collapsed on שבת, and the residents of the two courtyards had no shared עירוב.

phrases.english: Rav said:
One may not carry in it
except within four cubits.
And Shmuel said:
phrases.notes: This sets up שמואל's opposing view, which continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר, כּוֹתֶל שֶׁבֵּין שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵירוֹת שֶׁנָּפַל, רַב אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי quoted the rule that permission from the start of שבת remains, the גמרא brings a related dispute in which רב appears to disagree with that rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, when a wall between two courtyards falls on שבת, one may carry there only within four אמות. Permission from the start of שבת does not last.
